_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 'the Claude CLI stopped for a reason a retry on the
same subscription cannot fix' — the predicate that decides whether an automation
falls over to the free tier.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. This alternation used to be hand-copied into four places
docs/APEX_OPENCODE_HANDOVER.md) with a comment in each saying 'keep in lockstep'.
They drifted. On 2026-09-03 a SunBiz rep dropped a merchant application and got
'cli_failed:You've hit your session limit - resets 8pm' — the Node copy matched that
string, the Python copy did not, and the Python copy is the one guarding the
extraction daemon. The fallback never ran. A comment is not an enforcement
mechanism; a shared fixture plus a parity test is.
EVERY implementation MUST load this file (or, for a sibling repo that cannot,
IMPORTANT: this predicate is now an OPTIMISATION, not a safety gate. Callers must
fall back on ANY model failure (see scripts/lib/model_fallback.py and
scripts/integrations/extraction_consumer.py). This list only decides whether a
failure is worth retrying on the subscription first. A miss must cost latency,
_comment_v3: v3 (2026-09-12, Claude Spillover — see scripts/spillover/CONTRACT.md section 13).
lane_env_strip: env vars that every build_claude_spawn_env port removes from the
INHERITED environment before applying the caller's extras. A parent Claude Code
session exports CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli (which makes a child automation look
spill-eligible to the proxy), and a shell can carry ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or a model
lane override. No automation may inherit a route into the spillover proxy or a
lane. Each port keeps a FULL inline copy for an unreadable fixture, and the
parity test fails if a copy is missing a name.
subscription_limit_signals: the NARROW predicate is_subscription_limit() — the
account-wide usage limit is spent and every call fails until the reset. It opens
claude_cli's 30-minute quota breaker, so a false positive parks the whole fleet on
fallback models. Every signal is verb-anchored (hit / reached / exhausted / used
all, or a named '<kind> limit reached'): 'Approaching … usage limit' is only a
warning and a per-minute rate limit clears in seconds. The broad 'signals' list
above stays the retry-worthiness predicate; the two answer different questions.
